Real captures for spec 0303 R10 and R11 (issue #1941), taken before dep-audit.ts was written.
Each case directory holds `stdout`, `stderr` and `status` (the exit code) of one invocation.
Scrubbed: temporary directories became <venv>, <work>, <bin>, <npm-cache>; no user, host or
private index name remains. The text is otherwise untouched. No lockfile and no requirements
file is stored here (a vulnerable pin in the tree would raise advisories on the repository);
the inputs are described below.

npm 11.8.0, run with an empty user config and a fresh cache, from a root with a lockfile:
  npm audit --json --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts
  npm/clean       is-number 7.0.0                                     exit 0, no vulnerability
  npm/vulnerable  semver 5.7.1 (high) + cookie 0.4.0 (low)            exit 1, 1 high + 1 low
  npm/offline     same lockfile, npm_config_registry=http://127.0.0.1:9
                                                                      exit 1, stdout is a JSON
                                                                      object with a `message` and
                                                                      an empty `error`; stderr says
                                                                      "audit endpoint returned an
                                                                      error"
  Exit 1 means both "a vulnerability" and "the query failed": the two are told apart by the stdout
  JSON (`vulnerabilities` and `metadata`, or `message` and `error`), never by the exit code.

pip-audit 2.10.1 (pipx, Python 3.13.1), HOME on an empty directory (no HTTP cache), pip config
disabled (PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null; the host one points at an unreachable private index):
  The default invocation, `pip-audit -r req.txt`, BUILDS: pip-audit creates a virtual
  environment and runs pip on the requirements. With a requirement naming a source-only archive
  whose setup.py writes a marker file (`buildmarker @ file://...tar.gz`), the marker WAS written
  (pip/default-invocation-builds, exit 0). The default invocation therefore executes project
  code and is not used.
  The chosen vector, which builds nothing, is:
    pip-audit -r <file> --disable-pip --no-deps --format json --progress-spinner off
  With the same marker requirement the marker stays ABSENT (pip/url-requirement). `--no-deps`
  audits only the pins written in the file, not their transitive dependencies. With `--strict`
  added, a dependency that cannot be audited fails the run, so `--strict` is not part of the
  vector: the rules read the skipped entries instead (below).
  pip/clean                   six==1.16.0               exit 0, `vulns: []`
  pip/vulnerable              idna==3.6                 exit 1, 4 `vulns` entries holding 2
                                                        distinct ids (an id is repeated with a
                                                        second description): findings are
                                                        deduplicated by id. No severity field.
  pip/offline                 HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9, idna==3.6
                                                        exit 1, stdout EMPTY, a Python traceback
                                                        ending in requests.exceptions.ProxyError
  pip/offline-strict          same with --strict        identical
  pip/unpinned                `requests` (no pin)       exit 1, stdout EMPTY, stderr
                                                        "requirement requests is not pinned"
  pip/private-pinned          acme-internal-lib==1.2.3 (not on PyPI)
                                                        exit 0, stdout lists the dependency with a
                                                        `skip_reason` and no `version`; stderr
                                                        still says "No known vulnerabilities
                                                        found". A skipped dependency exits 0.
  pip/private-pinned-strict   same with --strict        exit 1, stdout EMPTY, stderr
                                                        "ERROR:... Dependency not found on PyPI
                                                        and could not be audited"
  pip/url-requirement         `buildmarker @ file://...`  exit 0, `skip_reason` "URL requirements
                                                        cannot be pinned to a specific package
                                                        version"
  pip/url-requirement-strict  same with --strict        exit 1, stdout EMPTY
  Consequences for the rules: exit 0 alone is never `clean`: a `dependencies` entry with a
  `skip_reason` is `not-audited`. Exit 1 is a vulnerability only when stdout parses and holds a
  non-empty `vulns`; empty stdout with a traceback is `offline`, with "is not pinned" is
  `unpinned`, anything else is `unrecognized-output`.
